clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HCLK: Single rising-edge clock per AHB interface. All signal timings are related to the rising edge of HCLK.
clock_and_reset_waveform_ahb.HRESETn: Active LOW. The only active-LOW signal in AHB. Resets the system and the bus.

clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PCLK: Rising edge times all transfers on the APB.
clock_and_reset_waveform_apb.PRESETn: Active LOW; normally connected directly to the system bus reset signal.

sequence: T0: Manager drives HADDR=A, HWRITE=0; HREADY=1 (previous transfer completed).
T1 (rising edge): Subordinate samples address + control. HREADY=1 means data phase begins.
T2 (rising edge): Subordinate drives HRDATA=Data(A); Manager samples on T3.
T1..T3: Address phase of next transfer (HADDR=B) overlaps the data phase of address A — pipelined.

ahb_waited_transfer_waveform.case: Read transfer with two wait states (Figure 3-3)
sequence: Address phase one cycle (HADDR=A, HWRITE=0).
Data phase extended over three cycles: HREADY=0, HREADY=0, then HREADY=1 with HRDATA=Data(A).
Effect: the address phase of the NEXT transfer (HADDR=B) is also extended (it must hold until the previous data phase completes).
Cycle 1: Subordinate drives HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=0 (signals start of ERROR).
Cycle 2: Subordinate drives HRESP=1, HREADYOUT=1 (Manager observes ERROR).
Manager may continue or cancel the burst. If cancelling, HTRANS=IDLE must be driven during the 2-cycle ERROR.
Address phase of the next (typically IDLE) transfer overlaps these cycles.

ahb_burst_waveforms.name: Undefined-length INCR (Figure 3-12)
ahb_burst_waveforms.note: Two undefined-length bursts shown; first burst ends, second begins with NONSEQ.

ahb_busy_transfer_waveform.case: Transfer-type example (Figure 3-6) — NONSEQ + BUSY + SEQ + SEQ + SEQ in INCR
sequence: T0..T1: NONSEQ at 0x20 — first beat of INCR.
T1..T2: BUSY at 0x24 — Manager unable to continue immediately; Subordinate provides Data(0x20) for first beat.
T2..T3: SEQ at 0x24 — Manager continues; Subordinate ignores the BUSY at T1 and reads at 0x24.
T3..T4: SEQ at 0x28 (third beat).
T4..T5: SEQ at 0x2C — Subordinate inserts a wait state (HREADY=0).
T5..T6: Subordinate provides Data(0x28); next beat continues.
Cycle 1: HTRANS=NONSEQ, HWRITE=0 (read), HADDR=A, HMASTLOCK=1.
Cycle 2: HTRANS=NONSEQ, HWRITE=1 (write), HADDR=A, HMASTLOCK=1; Subordinate provides Data(A) for the read.
Cycle 3: HTRANS=IDLE, HMASTLOCK=0; Manager presents Data(A) on HWDATA for the write.
T0..T1: IDLE (PSEL=0, PENABLE=0).
T1 (rising PCLK): PADDR=Addr1, PWRITE=1, PSEL=1, PWDATA=Data1 registered — SETUP phase.
T2 (rising PCLK): PENABLE=1, PREADY=1 registered — ACCESS phase; transfer completes.
T3 (rising PCLK): PENABLE=0; bus may go to IDLE or start next SETUP.
SETUP at T1.
ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0 (wait); PADDR, PWRITE, PSEL, PENABLE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT all remain stable.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=0 (wait).
ACCESS at T4 with PREADY=1; transfer completes.
SETUP at T1, ACCESS at T2 with PREADY=0.
ACCESS at T3 with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 — error signaled in the same cycle PREADY=1.
After T3: PSEL=0, PENABLE=0 (return to IDLE).

edges: IDLE -> IDLE on no transfer (PSELx=0, PENABLE=0)
IDLE -> SETUP when transfer required (PSELx=1, PENABLE=0)
SETUP -> ACCESS unconditional next rising PCLK (PSELx=1, PENABLE=1)
ACCESS -> IDLE when PREADY=1 and no further transfer
ACCESS -> SETUP when PREADY=1 and another transfer follows

max_outstanding_rules.ahb: AHB-Lite is single-Manager; only one outstanding transfer at a time (no AXI-style outstanding queues). Pipelining means address phase of next transfer overlaps data phase of current.
max_outstanding_rules.apb: APB has no pipelining; only one transfer in flight at a time; minimum 2 PCLK cycles per transfer.

interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_HREADY_chain: Multiplexor combines all Subordinate HREADYOUTs into a single global HREADY broadcast to Manager + all Subordinates (Figure 4-2). HRDATA, HRESP, HEXOKAY are mux'd by the decoder's HSEL selection.
interconnect_combination_rules.ahb_apb_bridge: An AHB-to-APB bridge is an AHB Subordinate and an APB Manager. PSLVERR maps back to HRESP=ERROR.

T0-T1 NONSEQ; T1-T2 BUSY; T2-T3 SEQ; T3-T4 SEQ; T4-T5 wait state; T5-T6 SEQ.
HMASTLOCK asserted across a NONSEQ-read + NONSEQ-write + IDLE sequence to the same address.
WRAP4, INCR4, WRAP8, INCR8, Undefined-length INCR burst examples.
Two-cycle ERROR response on HRESP: cycle 1 HRESP=1 HREADY=0, cycle 2 HRESP=1 HREADY=1.
PADDR, PWRITE, PSEL registered at T1 (Setup); PENABLE, PREADY registered at T2 (Access).
PREADY LOW during Access phase extends the transfer; PADDR, PWRITE, PSEL, PENABLE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT all remain unchanged.
Failing write transfer: PSLVERR asserted in the same cycle PREADY=1.
